input: a and b are ASCII strings. 1 <= len(a) <= 1000000 and 0 <= len(b) <= 1000000. a is never empty. Integers are plain int, excluding bool; lists and strings are ordinary list/str values rather than subclasses. Standard built-ins are unmodified; no concurrent mutation or custom field access occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The minimum nonnegative number of complete repetitions of a whose concatenation contains b as a contiguous substring, or -1 if impossible. Empty b returns 0. No repeated text or matched substring is returned.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs, caller-owned containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only a private prefix-length array is allocated. Repeated a is indexed virtually by modulo, without building a concatenated copy.
numeric: Prefix lengths and match lengths are at most len(b). The examined index is below len(a)+len(b)-1 <= 1999999. Modulo and floor division use positive len(a) and these small exact integers, so final repetition counts are exact. Empty b returns before any pattern indexing.
complexity: O(len(a)+len(b)+1) worst-case time and O(len(b)+1) auxiliary space. KMP scans only len(a)+len(b)-1 virtual characters: every possible match start is equivalent modulo len(a), so the first period covers all starts. The earliest completed match minimizes complete repetition count. Fallback steps amortize linearly; no quadratic string search or repeated concatenation is used.
